questions.q: Match the column: 1. .rtf 2. .odt 3. .pdf — a. OpenDocument text b. fixed print layout c. Rich Text Format
questions.solution: .rtf = Rich Text Format, .odt = OpenDocument Text (free office suites), .pdf = fixed print layout.
questions.shortcut: R = Rich, O = Open, P = Print.

questions.q: VLOOKUP searches for the lookup value in which part of the table?
questions.solution: **V = vertical search down the FIRST column**; the column-number argument only decides what is returned after the match is found.
questions.shortcut: VLOOKUP always enters from the left door.

questions.q: The minimum amount that can be transferred through RTGS is:
questions.solution: RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) is meant for large-value transfers - the floor is Rs. 2 lakh, settled individually and instantly. NEFT carries smaller amounts in batches with no minimum.

questions.q: A network confined to a single office building is classified as a:
questions.solution: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a room, building or campus. MANs span cities, WANs span countries/continents.
questions.shortcut: Local = LAN; City = MAN; Wide/world = WAN.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'The committee has approved these proposals.'
options: These proposals has been approved by the committee.
These proposals have approved by the committee.
These proposals were approved by the committee.
These proposals have been approved by the committee.
questions.solution: New subject *these proposals* is plural → **have been approved by the committee**. 'Has been approved' forgets to re-agree; 'have approved by' drops *been*; 'were approved' moves the row to the simple past.
questions.shortcut: Plural new subject → have been, never has been.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The teacher has said, "The exam will begin at ten."
options: The teacher has said that the exam would begin at ten.
The teacher has said that the exam will begin at ten.
The teacher said that the exam will begin at ten.
The teacher has said that the exam will be begun at ten.
questions.solution: The present perfect frame **has said** is still a present reporting verb — no backshift: **will begin** stays. 'Would begin' applies a past-frame rule to a present frame; 'The teacher said' downgrades the frame; 'will be begun' pushes a future simple into a passive.
questions.shortcut: has said is present too — the ladder is not climbed.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  HOSTILE
questions.solution: **Hostile** = showing enmity → unfriendly. The charge must stay negative.

questions.q: Which of the following questions can be answered from the passage?
options: How much does it cost to rent one beehive?
Why do some villages spray pesticides only in the evening?
Which apple variety needs the most bees?
In which year did wild bees start declining?
questions.solution: The passage says villages spray 'only in the evening, when bees are resting' — that answers the 'why'. It calls renting 'costly' but gives no figure, names no apple variety, and gives no year.
questions.shortcut: 'Costly' is not a cost figure — questions asking 'how much' need a number in the passage.
questions.passage:
Farmers in parts of Himachal Pradesh have begun renting beehives each spring. They place the boxes among their apple trees for a few weeks and return them after the flowers fade. The reason is simple: the wild bees that once did this work free of charge have become scarce.

Scientists point to several causes. Heavy use of pesticides kills bees directly, and orchards planted with a single crop leave few wild flowers to feed them once the fruit blossom is over. Warmer winters also disturb the match between flowering time and the insects' active season.

Renting hives helps, but it is costly, and the hired bees do not reach every orchard. Some villages have tried a cheaper approach: they leave strips of wild flowers along field edges and spray only in the evening, when bees are resting. Early results suggest that such steps bring wild pollinators back within a few seasons. The lesson is that nature's free services are free only as long as we protect them.

questions.q: The book ***Ghulamgiri*** (Slavery, 1873) was written by —
questions.solution: **Phule's *Ghulamgiri*** attacked caste slavery and the tyranny of the 'higher' castes.

questions.q: The Malabar coast lies mainly in which state?
questions.solution: West coast order north to south: Konkan (Maharashtra-Goa), Kanara (Karnataka), **Malabar (Kerala)**. Tamil Nadu has the Coromandel coast.

questions.q: Which of the following national parks was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985?
questions.solution: **Kaziranga**, **Manas** and **Keoladeo** were all inscribed in **1985**; the Sundarbans followed in 1987. Bhitarkanika and Kuno are not UNESCO natural sites.

questions.q: **Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt** won a Grammy (1994) for playing the —
questions.solution: His redesigned **slide guitar — the mohan veena** — won the 1994 Grammy with Ry Cooder for *A Meeting by the River*.

questions.q: A sum of ₹660 is borrowed at 20% per annum compound interest and repaid in 2 equal annual instalments. Each instalment is:
A dishonest dealer takes 10% more goods than he pays for while buying, and gives 10% less than the true weight while selling. His gain per cent is:
The simple interest on a sum of ₹10,000 is ₹1,200 for 2 years and ₹1,800 for 3 years. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.shortcut: The two SIs must differ by exactly one year's interest — ₹600.

questions.q: A batsman scores 45 runs on average in 8 innings. How many runs must he score in the 9th innings to raise his average to 50?
questions.solution: Required total $= 450$; current $= 360$; needed $= 90$.

questions.q:
Select the term that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**Z26, X24, V22, ?, R18**
questions.solution: Numbers are the letters' positions: Z26, X24, V22. Letters go −2 → T, whose position is 20. Answer **T20**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Milk, Water, Juice, Butter**
questions.solution: Milk, water and juice are **liquids**. Butter is a **solid** at room temperature → **Butter**.

questions.q: **Rita's son is Amit. Amit's wife is Sneha.** How is **Sneha related to Rita**?
questions.solution: Sneha is the wife of Rita's son → **daughter-in-law**. (Sister-in-law would need Sneha to be a sibling of Rita or of Rita's spouse.)
questions.shortcut: Wife of my child = daughter-in-law; parent of my spouse = mother/father-in-law.

questions.q: Five people **R, S, T, U and V sit around a circular table facing outward (away from the centre). S is to the immediate right of R, T to the immediate right of S, V to the immediate right of U, and R to the immediate right of V.** Who sits **immediately to the left of T** (from T's own perspective)?
questions.solution: Facing outward, right = clockwise. Chain the rights: R → S → T, and U → V → R, so the clockwise order is R, S, T, U, V. Facing outward, T's left is anticlockwise — the seat just before T — which is **S**.
questions.shortcut: Outward facing flips both hands: the 'left of T' seat is the anticlockwise neighbour.
